sentences.text: 1  THIS MSA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 54 OF LAND  ACQUISITION ACT, PRAYING TO ALLOW THIS APPEAL WITH  COSTS AND MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD PASSED BY  CIVIL JUDGE SENIOR DIVISION AT BALKI DATED 16-12-2010  IN LAC NO.120 OF 2001 AND ALSO JUDGMENT & AWARD OF  THE ADDL. DIST.
AND SESSION JUDGE AT BIDAR DATED  03.01.2015 IN MA [LACA] NO. 09 OF 2013 AND FIX MARKET
VALUE AT THE RATE OF `1,20,000/- PER ACRE AND AWARD
ALL STATUTORY BENEFITS AND GRANT ANY OTHER RELIEF.

-2-  NC: 2023:KHC-K:1119  MSA No. 200145 of 2017  THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

The land bearing Sy.No.68 of Kamalapur village of Bhalki Taluk measuring 4 acres 19 guntas was notified under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, on 21.09.1978 and thereafter an award came to be passed on 16.12.2010, by which a sum of `2,400/- per acre was offered by the Land Acquisition Officer.
2. The Reference Court on enquiry came to the conclusion that the claimant was entitled to a sum of `40,000/- per acre and in appeal the District Judge enhanced the compensation of `88,000/-.
3. Being dissatisfied the claimant is in appeal.

4. Learned counsel for the claimant contended that the claimant had raised both banana as well as chilly crops and as per Ex.P5, a certificate issued by the Horticulture Officer, a total of 1200 banana plants could be raised in an NC: 2023:KHC-K:1119 acre and yet the District Judge has considered the number of plants that had been raised at 1100 on the basis of a further assessment made in Ex.P.5.
5.
Learned counsel for the appellant also submitted that no assessment is made for the chilly crops that the claimant had raised and the multiplier of 10 applied would be inadequate.

6. As far as the second contention that the chilly crops were also raised along with bananas plants,
the same is not evidenced in the RTC and the RTC for the relevant period only indicates that banana plants had been raised.
In light of this evidence, the argument of the learned counsel for the appellant cannot be accepted so far as raising of chilly crops is concerned.

7. However, in respect of the quantity of banana plants that can be raised in an acre, the District Court has taken number as 1100 on the basis of Ex.P.5, but the District Judge has failed to notice Kashamma vs The Spl Land Acquisition Officer And Anr on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30064953/

sentences.text: 2 that the first column No.5 of NC: 2023:KHC-K:1119 Ex.P.5 the Assistant Director of Horticulture has himself stated that 1200 plants could be raised in an acre.

8. In my view since the RTC indicates that in the entire extent of land, banana plants were raised, it would be appropriate to accept that 1200 plants had been raised in each acre as against 1100 plants considered by the District Court.
9. The District Court has calculated the prices of each banana plant at `16/- and arrived at a sum of `17,600/-.
In my view the assessment of the value of each banana plant at `16/- cannot be found fault with.

However, since the quantity of banana plants as now been determined at 1200, the claimant would be entitled to contend that his income per acre would be 1200x16=19,200/- as rightly held by the Court, 50% of this is to be deducted towards cost of cultivation and the net income would be therefore be `9,600/-.

The argument of the learned counsel for the appellant that the multiplier of 15 would have to be adopted cannot be accepted since the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court that a multiplier by 15 should be applied to fruit bearing trees cannot really be applied to a banana plant.
11. In that view of the matter, the determination of multiplier of 10 cannot be found fault with.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of `96,000/- (9,600x10) as compensation per acre for the land bearing Sy.No.68 measuring 4 acres 19 guntas.
12. The appeal is accordingly allowed to that extent with costs.
13. As ordered on 15.03.2018, the claimant would not be entitled for interest on the period of 867 days which the delay in filing the appeal.
